title: VOCE Human Cognitive Assurance
status: VOCE public human-factors assurance framework; non-diagnostic and not a clinical instrument
purpose: Evaluate how agentic and digital systems shape attention, cognitive load, memory, verification, decision quality, fatigue and human oversight.
principles: Human oversight is effective only when the human can understand, notice and act in time.
Cognitive friction can be protective when it creates a meaningful verification step.
Automation should not silently remove the cues humans use to detect anomalies or uncertainty.
Cognitive controls are evaluated at the workflow and interface level, not used to diagnose individuals.
Evidence should distinguish laboratory findings, field observations, institutional inference and VOCE editorial synthesis.
Material changes to models, interfaces, alerts, permissions or task allocation can change cognitive risk and trigger reassessment.

domains.name: Attention & interruption
domains.description: Interruptions, switching, alerting and the ability to sustain or recover task focus.

domains.name: Cognitive load & complexity
domains.description: Information density, working-memory demand, multi-step execution and interface complexity.

domains.name: Verification & over-trust
domains.description: Checks, friction, confidence calibration and the risk of accepting fluent machine output without meaningful review.

domains.name: Memory & cognitive offloading
domains.description: What users must remember, what systems externalise, and whether critical knowledge remains retrievable and understood.

domains.name: Decision quality & uncertainty
domains.description: Uncertainty, missing information, anomaly detection and the conditions under which judgment is exercised.

domains.name: Fatigue & temporal load
domains.description: Decision fatigue, sustained monitoring, recovery, circadian constraints and workload timing.

domains.name: Human oversight & skill retention
domains.description: Whether humans retain comprehension, intervention capability and enough practice to take over when automation fails.

domains.name: Social & relational signals
domains.description: Loss or distortion of interpersonal cues in mediated, automated or compressed communication.

controls.title: Interruption recovery
controls.question: Does the workflow measure how quickly and accurately a user can resume a material task after an interruption or agent escalation?

controls.title: Alert saturation
controls.question: Are alerts prioritised and rate-limited so that critical signals remain perceptible rather than competing with routine notifications?

controls.title: Attentional handoff
controls.question: When an agent transfers control to a human, does the interface restore the minimum context needed to understand what happened and what requires attention?

controls.title: Working-memory demand
controls.question: Has the institution measured how many independent facts, states or pending actions the user must hold in mind at the same time?

controls.title: Context-switch burden
controls.question: Does the workflow minimise unnecessary movement between tools, agents, windows and representational formats during one decision?

controls.title: Information-density threshold
controls.question: Can a user identify the material facts, uncertainty and required action without parsing non-essential model output?

controls.title: Cognitive checksum
controls.question: Does every high-consequence action preserve a meaningful verification step rather than removing all friction in the name of speed?

controls.title: Confidence calibration
controls.question: Does the interface help users distinguish well-supported output from uncertain, incomplete or weakly grounded output?

controls.title: Automation-confirmation bias
controls.question: Has the system been tested for the tendency of users to approve a plausible machine recommendation without independently checking material evidence?

controls.title: Source-memory preservation
controls.question: Can users distinguish what they knew, what the system retrieved and what the model generated when revisiting a decision?

controls.title: Critical knowledge retention
controls.question: Does automation preserve enough human practice that essential procedural knowledge is still available when the system is unavailable?

controls.title: Memory expiry awareness
controls.question: Are users told when an agent's memory is partial, expired, reset or inconsistent with the current institutional record?

controls.title: Missing-information visibility
controls.question: Does the system explicitly expose material information that is missing instead of presenting an incomplete situation as complete?

controls.title: Weak-signal preservation
controls.question: Does digitisation preserve the contextual or interpersonal signals required to detect anomalies, manipulation or unusual cases?

controls.title: Decision latency fit
controls.question: Is the time allowed for human judgment proportionate to consequence, novelty and uncertainty rather than determined only by system speed?

controls.title: Sustained-monitoring burden
controls.question: Has the organisation tested how vigilance changes when humans supervise long periods of mostly correct automated execution?

controls.title: Decision-fatigue exposure
controls.question: Are repeated approval tasks batched, prioritised or redesigned so human oversight does not become a high-volume confirmation queue?

controls.title: Circadian and recovery fit
controls.question: For continuous operations, are high-consequence review duties scheduled with recovery and circadian constraints in mind?

controls.title: Takeover comprehension
controls.question: Can a human asked to intervene explain the agent's current state, objective, recent actions and remaining uncertainty before acting?

controls.title: Skill-atrophy control
controls.question: Does the operating model preserve deliberate human practice for skills that become essential when automation fails or is withdrawn?

controls.title: Meaningful override
controls.question: Is the human override understandable, timely and operationally effective rather than a nominal button available after consequences are irreversible?

controls.title: Social-cue loss
controls.question: Where judgment depends on interpersonal context, has the institution identified which non-verbal or contextual cues are lost through mediated or agentic interaction?

controls.title: Synthetic-interaction disclosure
controls.question: Can a person reliably tell when they are interacting with an automated agent and understand the limits of that interaction?

controls.title: Relational escalation
controls.question: Do sensitive or emotionally consequential interactions have criteria for transfer from automation to a qualified human?

review_triggers: Change in alerting or escalation logic
Change in staffing, shifts or supervision model
Observed rise in errors, overrides, fatigue or missed alerts
Introduction of synthetic social interaction in a sensitive context
clinical_boundary: The framework evaluates systems and workflows. It does not diagnose, screen, treat or profile an individual's mental health, cognitive disorder or neuropsychological condition.
